rationale: In credit card fraud detection, user spending profiles, merchant types, and adversary attack strategies change continuously. Random K-fold CV and IID train-test splits cause severe optimistic bias because identity features (card1, card2, addr1) overlap across folds, allowing models to memorize specific stolen cards rather than learning invariant fraud mechanisms.

calibration_window.purpose: Isotonic probability calibration and selective-escalation router threshold optimization strictly out-of-fold from model training.

test_window.purpose: Final untouched evaluation stream. No model hyperparameter tuning or router threshold fitting is permitted on this partition.

alternative_protocols_evaluated.name: Sequential 3-Window Rolling Backtest
alternative_protocols_evaluated.pros: Measures performance stability over consecutive quarterly cycles.
alternative_protocols_evaluated.cons: Smaller sample sizes for initial training windows.

leakage_verification_rules: Feature scalers fit ONLY on Train split
Target encodings fit ONLY on Train split
Calibrators fit ONLY on Calib split
Router thresholds tuned ONLY on Calib split
